summary: Solves the wheel-ground contact normal force for one contact. Rotates the wheel contact point (copied from the contact buffer at a2+76) into world space via the body rotation matrix at v3+28 (v3 = this[1404]), builds the contact-point velocity as a cross product of the rotated contact with the body vector at v3+124/132/140 plus the world angular velocity at v3+100/108/116, rotates the slip velocity back into the body frame, then when the normal slip component is negative (penetration) computes a friction-modulated normal force and an orthogonal damping force and accumulates the resulting angular momentum into the body via AccumulateAngularMomentum. Invoked per physics tick from DamperSpringForceComputationWithAntiRoll (0x004432F0) for each wheel corner.

local_names.this: suspension/vehicle object; this[1404] (+0x15F0) points to the chassis rigid-body sub-struct
local_names.a2: contact data buffer; byte 0 is the contact-active flag, +52/+60/+68 hold contact spring/damping/friction-reduction parameters, +76 holds the local contact position
local_names.a3: reference (road-surface) velocity vector; only components [0] and [2] are read
local_names.v3: rigid-body state pointer loaded from this[1404]
local_names.v4/v5/v17: cross-product terms of the rotated contact with the body vector (contact-point velocity due to rotation)
local_names.v16/v17: contact-point velocity vector after adding the world angular velocity
local_names.v18: reused buffer: contact local position, then body-frame slip velocity, then world-space contact force
local_names.v6/v7/v12: normal slip component, its square, and the squared-normal term
local_names.v8: sum of squared tangential and normal velocity components
local_names.v9: friction reduction factor built from the normal/total velocity ratio and the contact parameter at a2+68

operations.description: Guard: entire computation runs only when the contact-active flag byte at a2[0] is non-zero; otherwise the function returns immediately.
Copy the local contact position (3 doubles) from a2+76 into v18.
Load the rigid-body state pointer: v3 = this[1404] (this+0x15F0).
Rotate the contact position to world space: Matrix3x3VectorMultiply on the body rotation matrix at v3+28 (this+0x160C), writing the world contact position to v13/v14/v15.
Cross-product of the rotated contact position with the body vector at v3+124/132/140: v4 = v15*(v3+132) - v14*(v3+140), v5 = v13*(v3+140) - v15*(v3+124), v17 = v14*(v3+124) - v13*(v3+132).
Add the body world angular velocity (v3+100/108/116) to the cross-product terms to form the contact-point velocity vector: v16[0] = v4 + *(v3+100), v16[1] = v5 + *(v3+108), v17 = v17 + *(v3+116).
Rotate the velocity vector into the body frame via Mat3x3MulVec on the same body matrix at v3+28, writing the body-frame slip velocity back into v18.
Subtract the reference velocity from the slip: v18[0] = v18[0] - a3[0]; normal slip v6 = v18[2] - a3[2]. Only components [0] and [2] of a3 are consumed.
Guard entering the force-computation block: only when the normal slip v6 is negative (penetration / pressing), compared against the zero constant.
Compute squared velocity magnitudes: v7 = v6 * v6 (squared normal slip), v12 = v7, v8 = v18[0]*v18[0] + v7 (squared tangential plus squared normal).
Friction reduction factor v9: if v8 <= 0.0 then v9 = 1.0, else v9 = 1.0 - (1.0 - (v7/v8)*(v7/v8)*(v7/v8)*(v7/v8)) * *(a2+68). Uses the one-double constant pool value.
Force magnitudes: v10 = v9 * *(a2+52) * v12 (friction-modulated normal component from the spring parameter) and v11 = *(a2+60) * v12 (damping/tangential component).

Assemble the world-space contact force from the rotation-matrix columns scaled by v10/v11 (with the zero-constant matrix terms): v18[0] = v11*(v3+44) + v10*(v3+36) + (v3+28)*0.0, v18[1] = v11*(v3+68) + v10*(v3+60) + (v3+52)*0.0, v18[2] = v11*(v3+92) + v10*(v3+84) + (v3+76)*0.0.
Accumulate the resulting angular momentum into the body: AccumulateAngularMomentum with the world contact position (&v13) as lever arm and the assembled force v18.
Void return; no output values are written back to the caller.
